dnssecProposal.current: Enabled after separately approved recovery. Spaceship regenerated key tag 38997, algorithm 13, digest type 2, digest 90de957dae2de4145e548a4172e6a11ef5016c0094383e53c6a1934177bb6d77. Direct parent authoritative DS TTL 86400 seconds. Original source inventory retained key 23596 and recursive TTL 21600 as historical evidence, not a current migration gate.
dnssecProposal.requiredApproval: Founder approved DNSSEC disable only, then separately approved DNSSEC recovery after validating-resolver failure. No delegation or Cloudflare DNSSEC change approved. A future transition needs a new exact approval and supported preservation of old-zone signing through full parent DS cache lifetime.
dnssecProposal.sequence: Do not repeat ordinary Spaceship Disable as a proven zero-downtime method. It removed the zone DNSKEY and caused Google DNSSEC validation failure. Require supported DS-only removal with old-zone signing preserved through the current parent TTL, then authoritative DS absence and independent resolver/website/mail verification before separately approving delegation. After Cloudflare is active, enable Cloudflare signing and register only its actual DS with approval. Never carry a Spaceship DS to the new zone.
dnssecProposal.risk: A nameserver change with the stale old DS can break validating resolvers. No claim of instant DNS rollback.

applicationCutover: Separate later approval replaces both www Vercel CNAME and apex Vercel A with custom-domain associations to the same production Worker. All nine mail/service records and their TTLs remain unchanged. The existing www currently redirects to apex on Vercel, so retaining the apex website target after launch is unsafe for canonical routing. The new Worker redirects only the owned apex to www with uncached HTTP 307, preserving paths/query/method for rollback safety.
verification: Read complete authoritative Spaceship UI inventory, confirmed SRV priority/weight/port through authoritative DNS, read staged Cloudflare table values, TTLs and DNS-only states, and read actual Cloudflare-assigned nameservers. Google DNS-over-HTTPS still reports original NS/DS with authenticated data and the existing public homepage loads in the browser. The local Windows DNS resolver intermittently returned server failure, so its result was not used as evidence of a public outage.
